To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the divalent tracer Bis(ZnDPPA)-[111In]-DTPA was the most promising of three 111In-ZnDPPA tracers for imaging bacterial infection in a mouse leg infection.
all three 111In-ZnDPA tracer compounds were cleared rapidly from the body through normal pathways with no evidence of toxicity.
all three [111In] labeled zinc–dipicolyamine tracers selectively target the site of a mouse leg bacterial infection, with the divalent tracer exhibiting the greatest selectivity.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design of new radiotracers for SPECT imaging of infection, and the results of this work are a step forward in that process.
the development of a new class of bacterial targeting tracers for nuclear imaging of infection.
development of new imaging agents for detection of bacterial infection and this study provides a new lead for development of improved imaging agents.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the [111In]-Bis(ZnDPA) radiotracer has a very high potential to be used in clinical imaging of bacterial infections.
the divalent [111In]-Bis(ZnDPA) tracer is a promising new radiotracer for SPECT/CT detection of infection.
the divalent ZnDPA tracer was the most selective and promising candidate for further development.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the ZnDPA-[In-111]DTPA tracers are promising for in vivo imaging of bacterial infection.
a divalent [111In]-labeled ZnDPA tracer with a DTPA chelate is the best candidate for further development as a SPECT imaging agent for clinical detection and monitoring of bacterial infection.
the [111In]-labeled zinc–dipicoylamine tracers can be used to non-invasively image bacterial infections in living mice.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the divalent ZnDPA-[ 111In]DPTA tracer has the potential to become a useful tool for the diagnosis of bacterial infections.
a divalent ZnDPA-[11C]DOTA radiotracer may be a promising candidate for clinical translation.
the ZnDPA–DTPA and the ZnDPA-DOTA monovalent trac ers are not suitable for SPECT/CT infection imaging, while the bis(ZnDPA)–DTPA divalent tracer may have potential for clinical translation.
